newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Dexia Belgium shareholders seek to cash in.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dexia Belgium shareholders seek to cash in.

text.p: Belgium's cash-strapped local authorities, leading shareholders in Belgian-French banking group Dexia, have decided to cash in on the popularity of equity investments and will sell more shares in the group.

"It has been decided to sell a second tranche of Dexia shares as soon as possible because of the favourable stock market environment," Dexia Belgium chief executive officer Francois Narmon told a news conference on Wednesday.
The Brussels bourse, which is trading at all-time highs, has seen a flood of new issues and share placements in recent weeks.

Dexia Belgium has a 50 percent stake in Belgian bank Credit Communal de Belgique (CCB) and a 50 percent stake in French Credit Local de France. Dexia France also has 50 percent stakes in each of the operational banks, which specialise in credits to local authorities.

Belgian Holding Communal, itself 100 percent owned by Belgium's municipalities and provinces, sold a first block of Dexia Belgium shares in November 1996, as part of the cross-shareholdership alliance deal with CLF. That deal netted local authorities more than 32 billion francs.
A further sale of up to 15.5 percent this month will cut its stake in Dexia Belgium from 65.5 percent to just over 50 percent and raise another 20 billion francs.

Narmon said that most of the proceeds will go towards reducing local authorities' debts, which will help the Belgian public sector's effort in cutting debt ahead of European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
Formally, Holding Communal will offer 13.5 percent of Dexia Belgium shares, with a green shoe for an additional two percent.

A maximum price for the issue will be announced on June 14. After the June 16 to 23 subscription period, a final price will be announced on June 26, when the shares will start trading on the Brussels bourse.
Narmon said that the share sale will further boost liquidity of Dexia Belgium's shares, which should become eligible to join the Brussels bourse's Bel-20 share index.
"Based on a simulation on volume and capitalisation after the public offering, we consider that we are well-placed to be eligible for a place in the Bel-20," he said.
At the news conference, Narmon also said that the Dexia group plans to continue its foreign expansion and that it has a war chest of 60 to 80 billion Belgian francs.
"We have the ambition to continue our international expansion via takeovers or the acquisition of new activities," he said.
He added that Dexia sees growth possibilities on all European markets -- with the exception of its Belgian and French home markets -- notably in Germany, Scandinavia and Spain.
He said Dexia would remain a French-Belgian group which would take stakes in other banking groups, adding that he saw no widening of the core shareholding alliance between CCB and CLF.
Earlier this year, Dexia made a first move abroad when it took a 40 percent stake in Italian Crediop, a unit of Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino.
Crediop is the second-largest lender in the Italian public services financing sector.
Narmon was cautiously optimistic about about Dexia's 1997 earnings outlook and said that the 1996 alliance deal was benefitting from the first tangible synergy effects.
Dexia Belgium shares were quoted 3,780 francs, up 80, on the Brussels bourse. They started trade in November at 2,775 francs and reached a high of 4,150 in March.
